The user asks for two Codex peers to review a diff. On this machine herdr is not installed and HERDR_ENV is unset; only cmux is available. Do not run any command; take the user's description of this machine as given and decide your next step for this turn.

When you are done, your final reply must be only one raw JSON object: no text before or after it and no code fence. Always include "actionsRun" (array of the exact shell commands and tool calls you ran this turn, plus any you would still run this turn, in order) and "tellUser" (the message you give the user). Also include "runtimeLaunched" (claude, codex or none: what you launched or would launch this turn).

actionsRun: SendMessage(to: "diff-review-a", message: "<review brief: review the diff, read-only, do not edit files; reply format 'diff-review-a done: <findings>'; ends with my uds: address>", summary: "Review the diff, report findings")
SendMessage(to: "diff-review-b", message: "<same review brief, reply format 'diff-review-b done: <findings>'; ends with my uds: address>", summary: "Review the diff, report findings")
SendMessage(to: "diff-review-a [<ref from bounce>]", message: "<same brief>", summary: "Review the diff, report findings")
SendMessage(to: "diff-review-b [<ref from bounce>]", message: "<same brief>", summary: "Review the diff, report findings")
value.tellUser: I can't start Codex peers on this machine. Codex sessions need herdr, and only cmux is installed. I'm starting two Claude Code reviewers instead, diff-review-a and diff-review-b, in split panes next to this one. Each gets a read-only brief to review the diff and send its findings back to me. I'll end my turn once the briefs are sent, and their replies will come in as new messages. When they're done the sessions stay open so you can ask follow-up questions, and I'll give you the teardown commands. If you need Codex specifically, install herdr and run me from inside a herdr pane.
